## Purpose

Give Python API clients consistent prompt/cache usage across Chat, Completions, Responses and Messages. A cache miss does not prove a reusable write: this PR measures newly adopted prompt ranges and preserves the difference between **measured zero** and **unknown** through JSON and terminal streaming responses.

For K3, Responses and Messages `count_tokens` also use Chat's public prompt boundary, excluding the assistant-generation stub. This makes the APIs describe the same admitted input without changing physical cache metrics or traces.

## Design

Measure writes where the unified cache adopts reusable prompt ranges, carry cumulative measurements through the existing typed IPC, and project them at the API boundary with `--enable-cache-report`.

| Situation | Reported meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Newly reusable prompt ranges | Measured write count; earlier prefill chunks remain included. |
| Warm duplicate or normal non-disaggregated disabled cache | Measured zero. |
| Unsupported/unmeasured path, including PD decode | Unknown, even if decode's local cache is disabled. |
| Generated tokens, duplicate insertion or recomputation of an originally read prefix | Excluded from new writes. |
| Hybrid cache | Writes require a reusable state boundary. |

Responses records whether its numeric write field was measured. Messages publishes its measured input/cache partition in the terminal snapshot. Parallel choices keep writes unknown. API metadata bounds cached reads to the public input window while retaining main's `RequestOutputStats` carrier and per-output write updates.

This counts reusable cache admission. It does not promise retention, durable storage, billing policy or future residency. The separate Rust frontend does not report these writes. Includes #46549 and #46607; those smaller PRs remain open while this combined feature is reviewed. PD measurement transport is a follow-up in #48300, not an expansion of this PR.

## Validation

Current head: `23716525`, following the main merge at `240a7294` (main `3f5b1bec`). The latest commit changes only the transport test's `DisaggregationMode` import to its defining module.

| Source/path | Evidence | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current head `23716525`, CPU | The repository's indirect-import check and existing real transport regression pass. The regression covers IPC, cumulative snapshots, grouped/single-row routing, unknown/zero/positive values and native metadata. | No GPU serving was rerun. |
| Parent `240a7294`, CPU | Actual production modules pass focused meter/unified-cache, public usage, Responses JSON/SSE and Messages count-boundary checks. Grouped rows survive real msgpack with their original request IDs and write values. | Optional Rust-binding cases skipped. The full upstream multi-tokenizer module could not collect because the local HTTP-server import reaches an absent `mlx` package; the real splitter is exercised directly. |
| Historical October 31 CUDA E2E | One L20, TP1, Qwen3-0.6B **dummy weights**, BF16, Python radix, Triton attention and PyTorch sampling: real allocation, cache admission, scheduler, IPC and HTTP adapters. Cold/warm JSON and terminal SSE passed across all four APIs. | Pre-merge source. Not current-head GPU validation, trained-weight quality, full K3, distributed PD/hybrid serving, Rust behavior or performance. |

The CUDA checks assert exact full-prompt cold writes with a flushed dense cache and `page_size=1`, warm duplicate zero, stable writes across output lengths and consistent Messages counts. The meter and CUDA E2E sources are unchanged, but main changed surrounding serving code, so that result remains historical.

## CI and review

The parent revision's [lint failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41761849386/job/126351102775) identified the indirect import corrected by `23716525`. A [sampled Base GPU job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41761849714/job/126354858903) stopped at `Fail-fast: lint check failed`; it did not run the feature tests. New-head CI is assessed separately and is not yet claimed passing.

On the new head, [Base](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41767507015/job/126369455435) and [AMD](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41767506935/job/126369581399) were blocked by the per-user 120-minute trigger interval, measured from November 4 02:36:28 UTC. The `run-ci` label is present; these gate failures are not test execution. Lint was still running at readback. No repeated rerun was requested to bypass the interval.

Both original P1 concerns have reviewer confirmation in their existing threads: PD writes stay unknown and the CUDA assertions retain exact full-prompt write counts. Their resolved flags and formal maintainer approval remain separate. No additional review comment or rerun trigger is part of this description update.

+            cached = details["cached_tokens"]
+            self.assertEqual(usage["total_tokens"], prompt + output)

+        self.assertGreater(output, 0)
+        self.assertLessEqual(cached + written, prompt)
+        return prompt, cached, written

+    def test_cold_and_warm_usage_across_json_and_sse(self):

detail.body:
## Purpose

Give Python API clients consistent prompt/cache usage across Chat, Completions, Responses and Messages. A cache miss does not prove a reusable write: this PR measures newly adopted prompt ranges and preserves the difference between **measured zero** and **unknown** through JSON and terminal streaming responses.

For K3, Responses and Messages `count_tokens` also use Chat's public prompt boundary, excluding the assistant-generation stub. This makes the APIs describe the same admitted input without changing physical cache metrics or traces.

## Design

Measure writes where the unified cache adopts reusable prompt ranges, carry cumulative measurements through the existing typed IPC, and project them at the API boundary with `--enable-cache-report`.

| Situation | Reported meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Newly reusable prompt ranges | Measured write count; earlier prefill chunks remain included. |
| Warm duplicate or normal non-disaggregated disabled cache | Measured zero. |
| Unsupported/unmeasured path, including PD decode | Unknown, even if decode's local cache is disabled. |
| Generated tokens, duplicate insertion or recomputation of an originally read prefix | Excluded from new writes. |
| Hybrid cache | Writes require a reusable state boundary. |

Responses records whether its numeric write field was measured. Messages publishes its measured input/cache partition in the terminal snapshot. Parallel choices keep writes unknown. API metadata bounds cached reads to the public input window while retaining main's `RequestOutputStats` carrier and per-output write updates.

This counts reusable cache admission. It does not promise retention, durable storage, billing policy or future residency. The separate Rust frontend does not report these writes. Includes #46549 and #46607; those smaller PRs remain open while this combined feature is reviewed. PD measurement transport is a follow-up in #48300, not an expansion of this PR.

## Validation

Current head: `23716525`, following the main merge at `240a7294` (main `3f5b1bec`). The latest commit changes only the transport test's `DisaggregationMode` import to its defining module.

| Source/path | Evidence | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current head `23716525`, CPU | The repository's indirect-import check and existing real transport regression pass. The regression covers IPC, cumulative snapshots, grouped/single-row routing, unknown/zero/positive values and native metadata. | No GPU serving was rerun. |
| Parent `240a7294`, CPU | Actual production modules pass focused meter/unified-cache, public usage, Responses JSON/SSE and Messages count-boundary checks. Grouped rows survive real msgpack with their original request IDs and write values. | Optional Rust-binding cases skipped. The full upstream multi-tokenizer module could not collect because the local HTTP-server import reaches an absent `mlx` package; the real splitter is exercised directly. |
| Historical October 31 CUDA E2E | One L20, TP1, Qwen3-0.6B **dummy weights**, BF16, Python radix, Triton attention and PyTorch sampling: real allocation, cache admission, scheduler, IPC and HTTP adapters. Cold/warm JSON and terminal SSE passed across all four APIs. | Pre-merge source. Not current-head GPU validation, trained-weight quality, full K3, distributed PD/hybrid serving, Rust behavior or performance. |

The CUDA checks assert exact full-prompt cold writes with a flushed dense cache and `page_size=1`, warm duplicate zero, stable writes across output lengths and consistent Messages counts. The meter and CUDA E2E sources are unchanged, but main changed surrounding serving code, so that result remains historical.

The parent revision's [lint failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41761849386/job/126351102775) identified the indirect import corrected by `23716525`. A [sampled Base GPU job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41761849714/job/126354858903) stopped at `Fail-fast: lint check failed`; it did not run the feature tests. New-head CI is assessed separately and is not yet claimed passing.
